context.requirement_text:
Third and final part of ISS-0431/GH#835's fix, covering its own
explicitly-named SECONDARY surface: "Poller's per-tenant sweeps and
future LISTEN/NOTIFY work (ISS-0430) are secondary surfaces to cover
by the same decision rather than each inventing its own cap." Atop
REQ-216's core module; does not touch REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring.

WHAT `lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex` ACTUALLY DOES TODAY (read in
full, not assumed): `handle_info(:tick, ...)` calls
`Enum.each(schemas, fn schema_name -> Scheduler.poll_and_fire(schema_name)
end)` -- SEQUENTIAL, one tenant schema at a time, not concurrent. The
same sequential pattern repeats for
`maybe_run_retention_sweep/2`, `maybe_run_alert_detection/3`,
`maybe_run_ordering_cycle/1`, `maybe_run_ordering_sweeper/1`,
`maybe_run_ordering_metrics/1`. So THIS module does not exhibit
unbounded CONCURRENT demand the way the HTTP path does (each call
blocks the single Poller GenServer process, so at most one DB
connection is held by Poller work at any instant) -- the real gap
here is ACCOUNTING, not concurrency: Poller's one held connection is
invisible to REQ-216's admission budget, so REQ-216's global cap
(`pool_size - reserved_headroom`) can only be a safe ceiling on
HTTP-path concurrency if `reserved_headroom` already reserves enough
slack for Poller's own use -- an implicit, untested assumption today.
This requirement makes that assumption explicit and enforced rather
than merely documented.

SCOPE:
1. Before each of the six sequential per-tenant operations named
above (the timer poll-and-fire loop plus the five `maybe_run_*`
sweeps), acquire ONE global admission slot via
`Letflow.Admission.try_acquire(:global)` for that operation's single
Repo-touching call, and release it immediately after that call
returns (success or the operation's own already-established rescue
path -- do not weaken any existing per-operation try/rescue
isolation boundary documented in poller.ex's moduledoc, e.g.
`maybe_run_alert_detection/3`'s own `rescue _ -> :ok`; the
acquire/release wraps around the existing isolation, it does not
replace it).
2. On `{:error, :capacity}` from `try_acquire(:global)` for a given
schema's operation within a tick: skip that one schema's operation
for that tick only (do not crash the GenServer, do not skip every
other schema's turn, do not skip that schema's OTHER operations this
tick if a later `try_acquire` call for a different operation
succeeds) -- mirroring `fetch_tenant_schemas/0`'s own existing
per-tick-degrades-gracefully philosophy already documented in this
module's moduledoc, applied per-schema-per-operation rather than
per-tick.
3. Poller does NOT use REQ-216's per-tenant semaphore -- only
`:global`. Reasoning: Poller's sweep already iterates every tenant
schema once per tick by design (REQ-186's own decision), so a
per-tenant CAP on Poller would not bound fairness between tenants the
way it does for bursty HTTP traffic, it would only cause a tenant to
be silently skipped some ticks for no client-visible reason -- a
strictly worse outcome for a background sweep whose whole contract is
"every tenant gets a turn." Stated explicitly rather than left
implicit.
4. No change to `Letflow.Application`'s supervision tree (no new
process; Poller remains the sole caller, same GenServer, same child
entry) and no change to `Letflow.Scheduler`'s own `poll_and_fire/1`
contract (unchanged input/output; the acquire/release wraps its call
site in `poller.ex`, per §1 above).
NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT: no change to REQ-216's core semaphore or
REQ-217's HTTP-path wiring; no change to ISS-0430's future LISTEN/
NOTIFY work (named by ISS-0431 as a future secondary surface to cover
"by the same decision," not this requirement's own job to build); no
change to any `maybe_run_*` function's own internal per-schema
rescue logic beyond wrapping it in acquire/release.

task.description: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate (WF-02 Step 1b) on REQ-218's design (lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md). Verify insertion granularity against the real poller.ex source, resolve both design-flagged open questions (REQ-194 scope, mock/spy AC wording) directly rather than deferring, trace the after-clause release guarantee for correctness, check for literal implementation code, check the chosen Logger level against this codebase's own established precedent, and cross-check full AC coverage.
acceptance_criteria: with REQ-216's global cap artificially forced to 0 (test config override), a tick over 3 tenant schemas calls Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 ZERO times for any of them (each skipped for capacity), the GenServer does not crash, and the next tick (cap restored) resumes normally -- verified by a test asserting the mock/spy call count is exactly 0 during the forced-zero tick and exactly 3 on the following tick

with the global cap forced to admit exactly 1 concurrent unit, a tick still processes all 3 tenant schemas' timer poll-and-fire loop to completion (sequential acquire/release, not a permanent block), confirmed by observing all 3 schemas' poll_and_fire/1 calls occur within that single tick

an admission {:error, :capacity} for one schema's operation within a tick does not prevent a DIFFERENT schema's SAME operation, or that SAME schema's OTHER operations, from being attempted later in the same tick -- explicit test forcing capacity exhaustion mid-tick and observing partial, not total, skip

Letflow.Admission.try_acquire({:tenant, _}) is never called anywhere in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex -- grep-verified, confirming decision 3's per-tenant-exclusion is actually implemented, not just described

an existing per-operation rescue path (e.g. maybe_run_alert_detection/3's rescue _ -> :ok) still catches its own operation's raise with the new acquire/release wrapped around it -- a test forcing that operation to raise still leaves the admission slot released (no leak) and the tick completes
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary:
Read lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md in full against lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex (read live, not assumed) and docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-218 entry (all 6 ACs, verbatim). Six checks passed cleanly; one is a BLOCKER.

(1) INSERTION GRANULARITY -- CONFIRMED ACCURATE. Live-read poller.ex: the six named call sites match the design's §1 table exactly (line 107 poll_and_fire, no rescue; line 138 run_retention_sweep, no rescue; lines 152-158 build_context_and_detect wrapped in rescue _ -> :ok; lines 222-228, 237-243, 252-258 the three Ordering calls, each wrapped in rescue _ -> :ok). AC3's actual text ('a DIFFERENT schema's SAME operation... attempted later' + 'that SAME schema's OTHER operations... attempted later') is two independent sub-clauses, and each independently rules out a coarser wrap (whole-operation-loop; whole-per-schema-iteration) exactly as §3 of the design argues. No gap here.

(2) OPEN QUESTION 1 (maybe_refresh_active_instances/1, REQ-194) -- RESOLVED AS GENUINELY OUT OF SCOPE, no rework needed on this point. REQ-218's own requirement text is a closed, explicit enumeration ('the six sequential per-tenant operations named above') that lists poll_and_fire plus exactly five maybe_run_* functions by name -- it deliberately does not name maybe_refresh_active_instances/1, even though the requirement text was written from a full, careful read of poller.ex (it quotes the file's own function names in the file's own order) and that function sits sequentially between operations 1 and 3 in the real source (poller.ex:108). None of REQ-218's 6 acceptance criteria reference it or Engine.count_instances_by_status/1. Wrapping it anyway would be scope creep with zero AC coverage to validate it against (TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR would have nothing to check it against), and would contradict the requirement's own explicit six-item enumeration. The design's decision to leave it unwrapped and flag it for REVIEWER/ORCH as a possible follow-up requirement (not a REQ-218 gap) is correct.

(3) OPEN QUESTION 2 (AC1's 'mock/spy call count' wording) -- RESOLVED, design's proposed resolution is legitimate, no rework needed. grep -n 'mock|mox|Mox' mix.exs and the full deps list confirm zero mocking library in this codebase (ecto_sql, postgrex, plug, bandit, jason, telemetry, ueberauth_oidcc, lua, wasmex -- no mox/mock/meck). test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs's own established convention (per the design's §0/§6, confirmed by this codebase's broader no-mocking precedent) asserts real row-count/side-effect outcomes. AC1's literal 'mock/spy call count' phrase cannot be satisfied without introducing a net-new mocking dependency this codebase has never used -- itself a REVIEWER-flaggable new-dependency decision, not something TEST-DESIGNER should do unilaterally. The design's proposed substitution (assert the equivalent real effect is/isn't observed -- e.g. no timer fired vs. a due timer fired) preserves AC1's actual INTENT (verifying zero operations ran during forced-zero capacity, then verifying normal operation resumes) without weakening what is being verified. Legitimate interpretation, correctly flagged rather than silently substituted.

(4) RELEASE-VIA-AFTER-CLAUSE -- TRACED AND CONFIRMED SAFE, no gap. Proposed shape per §1 point 2: on {:ok, ref}, `try do <existing call, own rescue if any> after Admission.release(ref) end`. For rows 3-6, this nests an outer try/after around an inner try/rescue that already has `rescue _ -> :ok` (matching every raised exception). Elixir's `after` clause on a `try` runs unconditionally once the try block's body has run to completion OR an exception has propagated past it, per Elixir's own try/after semantics (unlike Java's finally analogy pitfalls, there is no path where after is skipped while the process is still alive) -- so release fires whether the inner rescue catches everything (the common case here) or, hypothetically, doesn't (belt-and-suspenders, as the design itself says). This is NOT analogous to REQ-217's register_before_send gap: that gap was about a callback that only fires on certain Bandit response-completion paths, an async/conditional hook; this is a synchronous try/after in the same process, which Elixir guarantees runs. For rows 1-2 (no inner rescue), an actual raise would still release cleanly via after but then continue propagating and crash the GenServer -- correctly disclosed by the design as an accepted, contract-documented risk (poll_and_fire/1's own contract already guarantees no raise), not a claim that after also prevents a GenServer crash. No misrepresentation, no gap.

(5) NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE -- CONFIRMED. Full read of lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md: one table (§1), prose walkthroughs (§2-§5), a test-approach narrative (§6), and open questions (§7) -- zero def/defp bodies, zero case/fn/-> control-flow fragments presented as real code, consistent with this run's own REQ-217 design precedent.

(6) LOGGING LEVEL -- BLOCKER, REWORK REQUIRED. The design commits, as a decided (not open) point in §2, to `Logger.info/1` for the capacity-skip log line, justifying it by analogy to fetch_tenant_schemas/0's 'degrade-gracefully philosophy.' I checked this against the actual codebase: (a) grep across lib/letflow/scheduler shows fetch_tenant_schemas/0 does NOT log anything on its :error path (only calls MetricsRegistry.mark_active_instances_refresh_failed/0) -- so it provides no real precedent for any specific Logger level, and the design's analogy to it is unsupported. (b) grep -rn 'Logger.info(' lib/letflow returns exactly one hit in the entire lib/ tree, and it is inside a design-doc code-comment example (req072), not real application code -- Logger.info/1 has no live precedent anywhere in this codebase. (c) The two real, on-point precedents for an 'expected condition, skip this one item, keep going' log -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex:37 and :44 (tenant not provisioned / schema missing, both skip-and-continue) and lib/letflow/obs/alerts.ex:588 (auth secret resolution failed, sending without Authorization, a degrade-and-continue path) -- both use `Logger.warning/1`, not info. `Logger.error` is reserved in this codebase for actual failures/exhaustion (alerts.ex:201 'alert detection crashed', alerts.ex:534 'alert delivery exhausted'), which a capacity skip is not. Given this task's own framing that an admission-driven skip is 'an operator-visible signal that capacity pressure is happening,' and given the codebase's own established two real precedents both choosing :warning for the same class of event (expected, non-fatal, skip-and-continue, worth an operator's attention), §2's choice of Logger.info/1 is not supported by precedent and should be Logger.warning/1 instead, OR the design must cite a real, on-point :info precedent if one exists that this check missed. This is a decided design commitment (not an open question left to ELIXIR-DEV), so it is in scope for this gate to fail on, per this run's own no-partial-credit rule.

(7) AC COVERAGE -- otherwise complete: AC1 (skip+resume) -> §1/§2/§6; AC2 (cap=1 sequential drain) -> §1/§3/§6; AC3 (partial not total skip) -> §3/§6; AC4 (no {:tenant,_} in poller.ex) -> §1 table + §6 grep-test description; AC5 (rescue still catches, no leak) -> §1 point 2 + §6; AC6 (mix test/compile) -> §6, correctly deferred to ELIXIR-DEV to run and quote.

issues.description: lib/letflow/design/req218-poller-admission-wiring.md §2 decides Logger.info/1 for the capacity-skip log line, justified by analogy to fetch_tenant_schemas/0's degrade-gracefully philosophy -- but fetch_tenant_schemas/0 does not log at all (verified: only calls MetricsRegistry.mark_active_instances_refresh_failed/0), so that analogy supports no specific level. This codebase has zero live Logger.info/1 call sites anywhere in lib/ (the only grep hit is a code-comment example inside a design doc, req072). The two real on-point precedents for an expected, skip-this-one-continue-the-loop condition -- lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning/backfill.ex:37,:44 and lib/letflow/obs/alerts.ex:588 -- both use Logger.warning/1. Change §2's decided log level to Logger.warning/1 (an operator-visible signal that capacity pressure is occurring, consistent with this codebase's own two real precedents for the same event class), or, if CODE-DESIGNER has a genuine on-point :info precedent this check missed, cite it explicitly by file:line in the revised §2 rather than an analogy to a function that does not log.
